title: Google Loses Fight Against Record €4.1 Billion EU Antitrust Fine
facts: Alphabet's Google lost its appeal against a record European Union antitrust fine regarding its Android operating system on July 2, 2026.
The European Commission initially fined Google 4.34 billion euros in 2018 for antitrust violations related to Android.
The European Commission penalized Google for forcing phone manufacturers to pre-install Google Search, Chrome, and the Google Play app store on Android devices.
A lower European tribunal reduced the initial Android-related antitrust fine to 4.1 billion euros in 2022.
The Court of Justice of the European Union is headquartered in Luxembourg.
The Court of Justice of the European Union fully dismissed the appeal brought by Google and its parent company Alphabet against the 4.1 billion euro penalty.
The European Commission previously fined Google 2.42 billion euros in 2017 for antitrust practices regarding its shopping comparison service.
Google officially lost an appeal against the 2.42 billion euro shopping comparison fine in 2021.
Google stated it adapted its agreements with phone manufacturers to comply with the initial Android antitrust decision back in 2018.
Google has accumulated close to 11 billion euros in European Union fines over the past decade for various antitrust infringements.
The record 4.1 billion euro European Union antitrust fine amounts to less than 3% of Alphabet's annual profit.
A Swedish court ordered Google to pay approximately 1.5 billion dollars in damages to the price comparison business PriceRunner.
The price comparison business PriceRunner is currently owned by the company Klarna.
The Swedish court issued the 1.5 billion dollar damage order against Google on Wednesday, July 1, 2026.
Google faces potential future fines under the European Union's Digital Markets Act regarding its search results and app store practices.
